about: scripts/ci/licenses.py: licences an MIT project may ship with, and reviewed exceptions (package -> its exact licence + why it is fine). A strong-copyleft (GPL/AGPL), source-available (SSPL, BUSL, FSL) or unknown licence is never added to 'allowed'; it is an exception only with a reason.

@img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64.why: libvips, the image library of sharp (next's image optimisation): an unmodified, dynamically loaded binary fetched from npm at install; AGOS does not copy or change it, which the LGPL allows for MIT code

@img/sharp-libvips-linuxmusl-x64.why: same library as @img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64, another platform build

@img/sharp-libvips-linux-arm64.why: same library as @img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64, another platform build

@img/sharp-libvips-darwin-arm64.why: same library as @img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64, another platform build

@img/sharp-libvips-darwin-x64.why: same library as @img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64, another platform build

sentry.why: dev-only: pulled by lighthouse 13 (@sentry/node -> @sentry/bundler-plugins) for the Lighthouse score test; never in the web build or the core, never redistributed by AGOS. Source-available (becomes Apache-2.0 two years after each release), not open source: drop it if lighthouse can be run without it
